analysis.title: The Icarus Files: What's next for Nvidia and AI
key_insights: Ten companies have been the largest in the S&P 500 since 1960. Nvidia rose fastest, from 1% of the index in December 2022 to 8.5% by May 2026. Most past leaders (GE, GM, Cisco, IBM, AT&T, Altria) fell to a small fraction of their peak share, and only Exxon still holds 1%+.

Nvidia's CEO leadership is changing, announced this week. Altimeter's Brad Gerstner and Atreides' Gavin Baker sent the board a letter asking for a 'deliberate process regarding the leadership of Nvidia that leaves all options on the table, including the return of Jensen Huang'. Nvidia now trades at the lowest valuation among large AI stocks by a wide margin.

Microsoft and Apple avoided the Icarus decline so far. Cembalest expects the same near term for Nvidia, which earned 83% of AI chip revenue in 2023-2025 at 75% gross margin and 66% operating margin. Nvidia's PEG ratio is 0.2x and its free cash flow margins have held while hyperscaler FCF eroded under debt-financed capex.

Cembalest calls competition for accelerators the most important section of the note. Nvidia has 39% of future frontier lab compute agreements (GW), against an 80%+ market share in 2023-2025. The rest is Amazon Trainium 24%, AMD GPUs 16%, Google TPUs 15% and Broadcom custom 6%, per the chart's legend order.

Epoch AI's inference performance index puts AMD's MI455X at the top per chip. A frontier lab said onboarding new models on AMD GPUs fell from 6-12 months to 3 days using its latest AI model for the engineering. This may erode Nvidia's CUDA and tokens-per-watt switching-cost argument. Nvidia's Rubin Ultra in 2027 may change that.
SemiAnalysis data on Qwen 3.5 397B shows Google's TPU7x beats the Nvidia GB300 NVL72 on cost per token at all but the slowest speeds.

Chinese open weight models consume the majority of tokens on OpenRouter and track closed frontier model performance. Nvidia is a direct or indirect supplier. SemiAnalysis estimates 1.5 GW of restricted Nvidia chips are already in China. IFP projects 32% of China's end-2027 compute will be remote access to US chips, mostly in Southeast Asia.

The Remote Access Security Act (RASA) passed the House 369-22 and has not had a Senate vote. It would let the US restrict Chinese firms from remotely using restricted chips overseas, with Asian cloud providers required to verify customers and obtain licenses. Cembalest says China hawks have the upper hand in DC.

Nvidia under Huang opposed US export controls and ring-fencing of China. Culper Research flagged Megaspeed (Singapore/Malaysia, funded and controlled by Alibaba per Culper) as an Nvidia customer. The share of Nvidia revenue billed to Singapore addresses rose from 8% to 22%, and Nvidia stopped disclosing it in July 2025.

Nvidia spent 58% of operating cash flow on equity investments and M&A over the last three quarters. Off-balance-sheet long-term debt and lease liabilities rose from $214bn to $422bn between Q1 and Q2 2026, and to $530bn including land, power and shell guarantees. The BIS says circular AI deals plus other AI-to-AI deals were over 50% of AI investment in 2021-2025.

A change in Nvidia's vendor financing could hurt neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius, Applied Digital and IREN, whose valuations are already down sharply this year. It could also weaken Nvidia's memory and logic wafer supply lock-up, helping AMD and Broadcom. Yields on AI infrastructure debt (HY and IG) have risen sharply this year and are weighing on overall high yield.

Nvidia's support for US open weight models (Reflection, Thinking Machines, Poolside) and its Nemotron model could fade. If RASA passes and works, Chinese firms get more incentive to build their own accelerators. Z.AI, DeepSeek and Meituan have already cited Huawei Ascend use in 2026.

Sell-side price targets implied about 40% one-year upside before last week's events. Baird cut from $500 to $200 (-60%), Evercore ISI $413 to $186 (-55%), Bernstein $315 to $200 (-37%), Citi $300 to $225 (-25%), JPM $280 to $215 (-23%), Goldman $285 to $220 (-23%), Morgan Stanley $288 to $267 (-7%), Wells Fargo $315 to $300 (-5%). UBS raised $280 to $300 (+7%).
Retail investors bought the 13% decline. Cembalest agrees Nvidia looks interesting for long-term holders at 32% below its all-time high and a 0.2x PEG. Its net debt to EBITDA is still below zero.

AI demand markers still look healthy: rising prices for legacy Nvidia GPUs, higher Taiwan and South Korea chip exports, and sub-1% US data center vacancy. The capex boom is the largest since the 1880s railroads.

Midterm voters showed near-universal support for data center restrictions such as capacity caps, zoning and water limits. If that cuts conversion of announced data centers in 2028, scarcer capacity could push owners to upgrade chips more often, which would help Nvidia.

sector_views.rationale: Nvidia's cash generation and valuation look strong, but its share of frontier lab compute is falling to 39% and AMD, Google TPU and custom silicon are gaining.
Neoclouds depend on Nvidia's debt, equity and lease backstops. AI infrastructure debt yields are rising and a change in Nvidia's approach could lift funding costs further.

earnings_insights: Nvidia earned 83% of AI chip revenues in 2023-2025 at 75% gross margin and 66% operating margin.
Retail buying also spiked in late February when Nvidia fell almost 10% after reporting Q4 revenues.
risk_factors: Nvidia leadership transition after the CEO change, with investors asking the board about returning Jensen Huang.
Frontier labs are moving compute to AMD, Google TPU, Trainium and Broadcom custom chips.
The Remote Access Security Act could cut off Chinese remote access to US chips, and a Congressional probe could focus on Nvidia's China-linked customers.
Nvidia's $530bn of off-balance-sheet commitments including guarantees, and its circular financing of AI firms, could lead to a retrenchment that hurts neoclouds and raises AI debt costs.
Rising yields on AI infrastructure debt are weighing on overall high yield markets.
Local data center restrictions after the midterms could slow capacity growth.

Epoch AI chart of modeled inference performance per chip ranks AMD MI455X first, ahead of Nvidia VR200 and GB300.
Chart of token output per dollar vs speed for Qwen 3.5 397B compares Google TPU7x at FP8 with Nvidia GB300 NVL72 at FP4 and FP8.
Table of Nvidia 1-year price targets since July 1, 2026 lists nine sell-side firms, with Baird -60% and UBS +7% at the extremes.
Chart of NVDA analyst price targets and stock price from July to November 2026.
Chart of Nvidia operating cash flow and its deployment into equity investments and M&A, Q3 2024 to Q2 2026.
vol_and_positioning: Retail investors were net buyers of NVDA during the 13% decline, per JPM Equity Strategy and Quantitative Research data through Nov 11, 2026.
Nvidia trades at 0.2x PEG, the lowest among the large AI stocks and sectors charted, and 32% below its all-time high.
geopolitical: The Remote Access Security Act passed the House 369-22 and awaits a Senate vote. It targets Chinese remote use of restricted US chips in overseas data centers.
US China hawks are ahead in DC on chip export restrictions, and Congressional inquiries may begin with Megaspeed, the Singapore company Culper says Alibaba funds and controls.

The note's header references an Iran war tracker, but the text does not discuss it. The note also mentions an FAA grounding of planes in the continental US and a Microsoft outage this week, without market analysis.

tension_points.bull_case: Nvidia has a 0.2x PEG, sustained free cash flow margins, net debt to EBITDA below zero, retail dip buying, and healthy AI demand markers such as rising legacy GPU prices and sub-1% data center vacancy.
tension_points.bear_case: The CEO change, a 39% share of frontier lab future compute, AMD and Google TPU performance and cost gains, China export restriction risk, and possible retrenchment from vendor financing that hurts neoclouds.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Senate passage of the Remote Access Security Act, or Nvidia scaling back vendor financing and equity investments to neoclouds.
